phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.description: Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens is Schenley Park's ticketed glasshouse and garden complex, with changing exhibits, its own schedule, visitor parking, cafe, restrooms and accessibility services.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.location: Use Phipps' GPS locator address, 700 Frank Curto Drive, for the Welcome Center. The conservatory sits beside Schenley Drive and Flagstaff Hill, not at the broad Schenley Park or Schenley Oval pin.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.parking: Phipps provides free visitor parking in the Schenley Drive center island, metered spaces on both sides, and accessible spaces near the entrance. Panther Hollow and Charles Anderson bridges are closed to vehicles, so follow the operator's current detours and allow extra time.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.hours: Open Monday-Thursday 9:30 a.m.-5 p.m., Friday 9:30 a.m.-10 p.m., and Saturday-Sunday 9:30 a.m.-5 p.m. Last entry is 30 minutes before closing; shows and visitor notices can close individual areas.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.restrooms: Visitor restrooms are inside the staffed conservatory. Phipps' sensory guide identifies restroom and quiet-space locations; do not rely on building facilities before admission or after closing.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.fees: Current general admission is $22.95 for adults, $20.95 for ages 62+, $19.95 for students 19+, and $13.95 for ages 2-18; members and children under 2 are free. Eligible EBT guests may receive Museums for All admission for up to four people at $3 each.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.accessibility: Most gardens are wheelchair accessible except the Stove Room. Manual wheelchairs and sensory bags are available free first-come at admissions, and accessible parking is near the entrance; stone and concrete paths can be uneven or slippery.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.dogs: Pets are not allowed inside Phipps. ADA-defined service animals are permitted.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.family: Allow roughly 90 minutes to two hours for a self-guided visit. Indoor and outdoor gardens work in mixed weather, but rooms vary in temperature and large bags, wagons and outside food are restricted.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.need: Advance timed tickets are strongly recommended and required during Holiday Magic. Tickets are nonrefundable, re-entry is not permitted, and nearby bridge closures change the normal driving approach.

schenley-plaza.description: Schenley Plaza is the park's level Oakland gathering lawn, carousel and food-stop zone between Carnegie Library, Phipps and the university district.
schenley-plaza.sourceLabel: Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy Schenley entrances guide
schenley-plaza.location: Navigate to Schenley Plaza at Forbes Avenue and Schenley Drive. It is the north Oakland edge of the larger park, across from Carnegie Library and downhill from Flagstaff Hill.
schenley-plaza.parking: The Conservancy identifies parallel and head-in street parking around the plaza. Read meter and event restrictions carefully; university activity and Phipps traffic can fill the immediate spaces.
schenley-plaza.hours: The outdoor plaza follows posted City park hours. The PNC Carousel, The Porch, kiosks, rentals and events use separate seasonal or daily schedules.
schenley-plaza.restrooms: Do not assume an always-open public restroom in the lawn. Use an open staffed plaza business, library, museum or Phipps only under that operator's access rules and hours.
schenley-plaza.fees: Ordinary lawn, seating and path access is free. Carousel rides, food, rentals and ticketed or reserved events cost separately.
schenley-plaza.accessibility: The central plaza has broad paved walks and a relatively level lawn-edge route, but curb cuts, temporary event furniture, grass and crowding can affect movement.
schenley-plaza.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor plaza areas under City rules. Keep pets out of food-service seating, the carousel and any posted or event-controlled zone.
schenley-plaza.family: The open lawn, seasonal carousel and nearby food can make an easy family stop. Confirm carousel operation and plan a restroom before settling in.
schenley-plaza.need: Treat the plaza, carousel and food operators as separate schedules. A quiet lawn visit can change quickly during university events, festivals or rentals.

panther-hollow-lake.description: Panther Hollow Lake is the small man-made lake beneath the park's bridges, reached by trail and steps rather than as a drive-up waterfront destination.
panther-hollow-lake.address: Panther Hollow Trail, Schenley Park, Pittsburgh, PA 15213
panther-hollow-lake.sourceLabel: Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy Schenley entrances guide
panther-hollow-lake.location: The lake sits below Phipps, Flagstaff Hill and Panther Hollow Road. Anderson Playground is a practical upper arrival for steps down toward the lake; use the exact lake pin and expect a climb back out.
panther-hollow-lake.parking: Use legal two-hour parking near Anderson Playground or another mapped Schenley entrance, then continue on foot. There is no lakefront parking lot and closed bridges can alter vehicle circulation.
panther-hollow-lake.hours: Visit the lake and connecting natural trails in daylight under posted park and trail rules. Flooding, mud, ice, fallen trees and maintenance can close or complicate the approach.
panther-hollow-lake.restrooms: There is no dependable restroom at the lake. Use an open staffed facility before descending into Panther Hollow.
panther-hollow-lake.fees: Trail and lake-view access is free. This is not a staffed boating, swimming or rental facility.
panther-hollow-lake.accessibility: The hollow approach includes steep grades, steps and natural surfaces and is not a step-free lake visit. Choose Schenley Plaza or another developed park destination when a firm level route is essential.
panther-hollow-lake.dogs: Leashed dogs may use open trails under City rules. Keep animals out of the water and under close control on steep, muddy and narrow sections.
panther-hollow-lake.family: The lake can be a short nature destination for trail-ready children, but steep access, rail infrastructure, water and limited facilities require close supervision.
panther-hollow-lake.need: This is a trail destination, not a swimming lake or drive-up picnic area. Download the park map, visit in daylight and avoid the hollow during thunderstorms, flooding, snow or ice.

flagstaff-hill.description: Flagstaff Hill is the broad slope and skyline viewpoint directly above Phipps, used for picnics, sledding, films and informal gatherings.
flagstaff-hill.sourceLabel: Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy Schenley entrances guide
flagstaff-hill.location: Flagstaff Hill rises across Schenley Drive from Phipps and southeast of Schenley Plaza. Use the exact hill pin rather than routing to the Oval or Panther Hollow Lake.
flagstaff-hill.parking: Use legal spaces along Schenley Drive and the Phipps area, honoring meters, bike-lane markings and event restrictions. Phipps visitor spaces are intended for conservatory guests, not an all-day hill visit.
flagstaff-hill.hours: Use the open hill during posted City park hours. Films, festivals, university events, snow conditions and maintenance can create separate access or crowd controls.
flagstaff-hill.restrooms: There is no dependable dedicated restroom on the hill. Phipps restrooms require admission and follow conservatory hours; plan another open facility before arriving.
flagstaff-hill.fees: Ordinary hill, picnic and skyline-view access is free. Permitted events, food and nearby attractions may charge separately.
flagstaff-hill.accessibility: The defining lawn is sloped and grassy. Paved roadside viewpoints may provide partial context, but the hill itself is not a level or uniformly firm destination.
flagstaff-hill.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the open hill under City rules. Avoid event-controlled areas and clean up waste on the heavily shared lawn.
flagstaff-hill.family: The skyline, open grass and proximity to Phipps make a flexible family stop. Supervise children beside Schenley Drive and on the steep slope, especially during snow or crowded events.
flagstaff-hill.need: Bring shade and water in summer and traction in winter. The open slope is exposed to sun, wind, lightning and snow, and event programming can replace normal informal use.

frick-environmental-center.description: Frick Environmental Center is the park's free public nature-education building and most useful first-stop arrival, with maps, programs, parking, bathrooms, water fountains and developed access to nearby trails.
frick-environmental-center.location: Navigate to 2005 Beechwood Boulevard and enter between the historic stone gatehouses. The modern center sits beyond the entrance landscape; it is not the Blue Slide, Forbes and Braddock or Nine Mile Run arrival.
frick-environmental-center.parking: Parking is available at the Environmental Center. Current ranger guidance uses the space between the two gatehouses as the trail-meeting point; arrive early for programs and do not assume the small lot can absorb major-event traffic.
frick-environmental-center.hours: The published building schedule is Monday-Friday 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m., Saturday 10:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. and Sunday noon-5:00 p.m. Programs, holidays, rentals, maintenance and severe weather can alter access, so verify the current calendar.
frick-environmental-center.restrooms: Bathrooms and water fountains are documented at the center during building access. They are the most dependable starting facilities before a ravine walk, but they are not available after the building closes.
frick-environmental-center.fees: Ordinary public building and park access is free. Camps, classes, special programs, private rentals and reserved events may charge.
frick-environmental-center.accessibility: The center and its developed arrival provide the park's strongest firm-surface option. The City is evaluating additional ADA upgrades in 2026; nearby nature routes still vary in slope and surface, so follow posted accessible routing.
frick-environmental-center.dogs: Leashed dogs may use open outdoor park routes, but building access and programs can restrict animals. Only ADA-defined service animals should be assumed inside; use the separate signed Upper Frick off-leash area for unleashed play.
frick-environmental-center.family: The free living-building exhibits, bathrooms, water, programs and short nearby routes make this the easiest family orientation point. Confirm program registration and bring trail shoes for any walk beyond the developed campus.
frick-environmental-center.need: The building schedule is narrower than park hours. Treat the center, education programs and outdoor trails as separate operating surfaces, and check the current calendar before relying on indoor facilities.

nine-mile-run-trail.description: Nine Mile Run Trail follows Pittsburgh's restored urban stream corridor through lower Frick Park, but the Commercial Street Bridge replacement is changing and closing sections of the normal route in 2026.
nine-mile-run-trail.address: Nine Mile Run Trail Parking, Pittsburgh, PA 15218
nine-mile-run-trail.location: Use the exact trail point near Commercial Street only after reading current construction notices. Nine Mile Run extends south toward Duck Hollow and north into Frick's trail network; it is not reached from the Environmental Center without a substantial trail connection.
nine-mile-run-trail.parking: Commercial Street and Duck Hollow have served different ends of the corridor, but the bridge project can close lots and the connection between them. Follow PennDOT signs and do not park in work zones or assume a through-route exists.
nine-mile-run-trail.hours: Use the natural corridor in daylight and obey posted construction closures. Work windows, flooding, storms, ice, fallen trees and restoration activity can close the trail independently of broad park hours.
nine-mile-run-trail.restrooms: There is no dependable staffed restroom along the lower corridor. Use an open facility before arriving and carry water; construction may also affect portable or nearby options.
nine-mile-run-trail.fees: Trail access is free. This is an unstaffed public greenway, not a paid attraction or rental facility.
nine-mile-run-trail.accessibility: The corridor includes crushed gravel, boardwalk or bridge segments and construction detours. Conditions, grades and surfaces vary, and the active project means no continuous step-free route should be assumed without a same-day operator check.
nine-mile-run-trail.dogs: Leashed dogs may use open trail sections under City rules. Keep dogs out of the stream and restoration areas and under close control near cyclists, narrow passages and construction fencing.
nine-mile-run-trail.family: The stream restoration and relatively gentle lower corridor can interest trail-ready children, but road crossings, water, bikes, limited facilities and active construction require close supervision and a clear turnaround plan.
nine-mile-run-trail.need: PennDOT's Commercial Street Bridge replacement is an active, time-sensitive constraint. Confirm which trail segment and parking area are open before leaving; never cross a barricade to complete a planned through-walk or ride.

point-state-park-fountain.description: Point State Park Fountain is the park's 100-foot landmark at the Forks of the Ohio, reached by continuing west from the Commonwealth Place entrance across the lawn and paved riverfront promenades.
point-state-park-fountain.address: Point State Park Fountain, Pittsburgh, PA 15222
point-state-park-fountain.location: The fountain is at the far western tip of the park where the Allegheny and Monongahela form the Ohio River. Enter from Commonwealth Place and continue beyond the Portal Bridge, museum, Block House and main lawn; the fountain pin is not the vehicle entrance or parking lot.
point-state-park-fountain.parking: Use the paid Commonwealth Place lot, limited legal meters or a downtown garage, then walk through the park. There is no fountain-side visitor parking, and major events can close the lot or control the final approach.
point-state-park-fountain.hours: The surrounding park is open sunrise to sunset. DCNR turned the fountain on April 8 for the 2026 season after completing upgrades, but water operation remains separate from park access and can pause for weather, maintenance, water conditions or events.
point-state-park-fountain.restrooms: The official park map places modern restrooms and potable water near the entrance and park office, not at the fountain tip. Use those facilities before crossing the lawn and do not assume the concession or museum will be open.
point-state-park-fountain.fees: Viewing the fountain and confluence is free, and Pennsylvania state parks have no day-use admission fee. Parking, food, museum admission and special events may cost separately.
point-state-park-fountain.accessibility: DCNR identifies the paved riverfront promenades and overlooks as accessible. The route from the entrance to the fountain is firm and largely level, but it is an exposed walk and temporary event barriers can alter the path.
point-state-park-fountain.dogs: Physically controlled pets may use open state-park day-use areas unless posted closed. Keep pets out of the fountain basin, clean up waste and avoid building interiors; ordinary pets are not admitted inside park buildings.
point-state-park-fountain.family: The spray and river traffic are visually engaging, but the fountain is ornamental rather than a splash pad. Supervise children beside the basin and three active rivers, and plan shade, water and a restroom stop before the exposed final lawn.
point-state-park-fountain.need: Do not plan on entering the fountain basin or treating it as water play. Confirm same-day DCNR alerts and fountain operation, especially during storms, maintenance or large downtown events.

fort-pitt-museum.description: Fort Pitt Museum is Point State Park's ticketed two-floor history museum, interpreting the French and Indian War, the American Revolution and the founding of Pittsburgh through exhibits, artifacts and seasonal programs.
fort-pitt-museum.address: Point State Park, 601 Commonwealth Place, Pittsburgh, PA 15222
fort-pitt-museum.sourceLabel: Heinz History Center Fort Pitt Museum
fort-pitt-museum.location: Enter Point State Park from Commonwealth Place and cross beneath the Portal Bridge. The museum is the staffed building near the park entrance, opposite the Block House; it is well before the fountain at the western tip.
fort-pitt-museum.parking: The museum owns no parking lot. Its operator lists the paid Boulos lot, metered spaces and several downtown garages, all requiring a walk; route to Point State Park's Commonwealth Place entrance rather than trying to drive to the museum door.
fort-pitt-museum.hours: Regular museum hours are daily 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. It closes on New Year's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving and Christmas, and major Point State Park events can add date-specific closures; verify the operator calendar before leaving.
fort-pitt-museum.restrooms: An accessible restroom is on the museum's first floor and is available during admission hours. Do not rely on it before the museum opens or after it closes; the park also has separate modern restrooms near the entrance.
fort-pitt-museum.fees: Current general admission is $10 for adults, $8 for ages 65+, and $6 for students with valid school ID. Visitors 17 and under are free but still need tickets; members are free and military, RAD Pass and combination-ticket programs have separate terms.
fort-pitt-museum.accessibility: The entrance has an ADA push-button opener, galleries are wheelchair accessible, an elevator connects floors, videos include captions and an accessible restroom is on the first floor. A manual wheelchair and sensory bags are available first-come.
fort-pitt-museum.dogs: Ordinary pets and emotional-support animals are not admitted. ADA-defined service animals are welcome and must remain under control.
fort-pitt-museum.family: Children 17 and under receive free general admission but still need tickets. Interactive exhibits, artifacts and seasonal living-history demonstrations can pair well with the outdoor fort outlines; check event times and allow for security or crowd controls.
fort-pitt-museum.need: The museum has its own ticket, holiday and event-closure rules even when the park is open. Reserve tickets when timing matters and check the operator notice before a major downtown event.

fort-pitt-block-house.description: Fort Pitt Block House is the free, small 1764 historic site opposite Fort Pitt Museum, preserving the only surviving structure from Fort Pitt and interpreting it through on-site exhibits and educators.
fort-pitt-block-house.address: 601 Commonwealth Place, Building C, Pittsburgh, PA 15222
fort-pitt-block-house.location: Enter Point State Park from Commonwealth Place and pass beneath the Portal Bridge. The Block House is directly across from Fort Pitt Museum and close to the entrance-side fort grounds; it is not at the fountain tip.
fort-pitt-block-house.parking: Use the same paid Commonwealth Place lot, legal meters or downtown garages used for Point State Park. The site is reached on foot beyond the Portal Bridge and has no dedicated visitor parking at the building.
fort-pitt-block-house.hours: From April 1 through October 31, it is open Wednesday-Saturday 10:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m. From November 1 through March 31, it is open Friday-Saturday 10:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m. Hours are subject to change and group tours can require arrangements.
fort-pitt-block-house.restrooms: The operator does not document a dedicated public restroom inside this small historic building. Use Point State Park's modern restroom near the entrance, or Fort Pitt Museum only during its ticketed operating hours.
fort-pitt-block-house.fees: Admission is free. Tours, group arrangements, souvenirs and donations are separate, and parking still costs unless arriving by transit, walking or bicycle.
fort-pitt-block-house.accessibility: The surrounding memorial garden has wide paths and seating, but this is a compact 1764 structure and the upstairs is closed for preservation and safety. Contact the operator before visiting when step-free entry, turning space or another accommodation is essential.
fort-pitt-block-house.dogs: State-park rules permit physically controlled pets in open day-use areas but prohibit ordinary pets inside buildings. Keep pets outside the historic structure and contact the operator directly about service-animal or accommodation needs.
fort-pitt-block-house.family: The free site is small enough for a short family stop and includes exhibits, digital presentations and a reconstructed firing step. The historic interior and original fabric require close supervision, and the second floor is not open to visitors.
fort-pitt-block-house.need: The Block House is free but not open daily. Check the seasonal Wednesday-Saturday or Friday-Saturday schedule before crossing the park, and do not assume its hours match Fort Pitt Museum or the outdoor grounds.
